title: Numbers 4:21–33
context: Numbers 4:21–33 gives the census instructions and duties for the Gershonites and Merarites. The Gershonites carry the fabrics (curtains, coverings, screens, and hangings), and the Merarites carry the frame (boards, bars, pillars, sockets, pins, and cords). Both clans work under Ithamar son of Aaron. Arminian and Reformed readers agree that the passage shows God valuing every kind of service and assigning it in an orderly way under appointed oversight.

verses.text: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.arminianNotes: A divine speech introduces the Gershonite census. Arminians see God continuing to order every part of the service. The Gershonites’ duties come next, after the Kohathites’ more dangerous work has been arranged.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed interpreters agree. Both traditions agree on the function of the verse. The same formula introduced the Kohathite instructions in verse 1, which ties the sections together.

verses.text: “Take a census of the sons of Gershon also, by their fathers’ houses, by their families;
verses.arminianNotes: The Gershonites are counted by fathers’ houses and families. Arminians see each family included in God’s plan. The wording repeats verse 2 so that every clan is organized the same way.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree. Both traditions read the verse as procedural and agree on it. Counting by fathers’ houses reflects Israel’s family-based social structure.

verses.text: you shall count them from thirty years old and upward until fifty years old: all who enter in to wait on the service, to do the work in the Tent of Meeting.
verses.arminianNotes: Men from thirty to fifty who serve in the Tent of Meeting are counted. Arminians see the same standard applied consistently to each clan.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed interpreters agree. Both traditions agree on the verse. The phrase ‘to wait on the service’ may carry a military image of serving in ranks, though interpreters differ on how much to make of it.

verses.text: “This is the service of the families of the Gershonites, in serving and in bearing burdens:
verses.arminianNotes: The Gershonites’ service is ‘in serving and in bearing burdens’. Arminians see faithful labor, even carrying loads, as service to God.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree that ordinary labor offered in God’s service honors him. Both traditions agree on the verse. ‘Bearing burdens’ shows that physical labor was a recognized form of sacred duty.

verses.text: they shall carry the curtains of the tabernacle and the Tent of Meeting, its covering, the covering of sealskin that is on it, the screen for the door of the Tent of Meeting,
verses.arminianNotes: They carry the curtains, tent, coverings, and entrance screen. Arminians see trusted responsibility for the tabernacle’s fabrics.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed interpreters agree. Both traditions read the verse as procedural and agree on it. These fabrics were the visible coverings, so the Gershonites handled what onlookers would see of the tabernacle.

verses.text: the hangings of the court, the screen for the door of the gate of the court which is by the tabernacle and around the altar, their cords, and all the instruments of their service, and whatever shall be done with them. They shall serve in there.
verses.arminianNotes: They also carry the court hangings, gate screen, cords, and instruments, and ‘serve in there’. Arminians see thorough, faithful service.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree. Both traditions read the verse as completing the Gershonite list and agree on it. The list repeats 3:25–26 almost exactly, which confirms that the Gershonite duties were consistent.

verses.text: At the commandment of Aaron and his sons shall be all the service of the sons of the Gershonites, in all their burden and in all their service; and you shall appoint their duty to them in all their responsibilities.
verses.arminianNotes: Their work is under the direction of Aaron and his sons. Arminians see willing service under appointed leadership. The priests’ direction ensured that the Levites knew exactly what to carry.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed interpreters agree that the verse establishes ordered authority. Both traditions agree on its meaning. The priests appointed the tasks, so no Levite needed to guess his duty.

verses.text: This is the service of the families of the sons of the Gershonites in the Tent of Meeting. Their duty shall be under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.
verses.arminianNotes: The Gershonites serve under Ithamar son of Aaron. Arminians see accountable oversight provided for every group. Ithamar’s oversight spreads responsibility among Aaron’s surviving sons.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree. Both traditions note that Ithamar also oversaw the tabernacle accounts (Exodus 38:21) and agree on the verse.

verses.text: “As for the sons of Merari, you shall count them by their families, by their fathers’ houses;
verses.arminianNotes: The Merarites are counted by families and fathers’ houses. Arminians see God’s care extending to each clan. The Merarites are counted on the same basis as the other clans.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed interpreters agree. Both traditions read the verse as procedural and agree on it. The verse repeats the structure of verses 2 and 22 so that the census is uniform.

verses.text: you shall count them from thirty years old and upward even to fifty years old—everyone who enters on the service, to do the work of the Tent of Meeting.
verses.arminianNotes: Men from thirty to fifty who serve are counted. Arminians note the same consistent standard. The age range from thirty to fifty matches that of the other two clans.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree. Both traditions agree on the verse. The uniform standard ensures that the heaviest work is done by mature men.

verses.text: This is the duty of their burden, according to all their service in the Tent of Meeting: the tabernacle’s boards, its bars, its pillars, its sockets,
verses.arminianNotes: The Merarites carry the boards, bars, pillars, and sockets. Arminians see heavy work honored as part of worship. The Merarites’ loads were the heaviest of the tabernacle’s parts.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed interpreters agree. Both traditions note that 7:8 later provides wagons for this heavy load and agree on the verse.

verses.text: the pillars of the court around it, their sockets, their pins, their cords, with all their instruments, and with all their service. You shall appoint the instruments of the duty of their burden to them by name.
verses.arminianNotes: The court pillars, sockets, pins, and cords are assigned ‘by name’. Arminians see personal responsibility for specific items.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers agree that assigning items by name promotes accountability. Both traditions agree on the verse. Naming the items prevented confusion or loss during the frequent moves in the wilderness.

verses.text: This is the service of the families of the sons of Merari, according to all their service in the Tent of Meeting, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.”
verses.arminianNotes: The Merarites serve under Ithamar. Arminians see the same accountable oversight. Gershon and Merari both work under Ithamar, while Eleazar oversees the Kohathites’ holy things (4:16).
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed interpreters agree. Both traditions read the verse as closing the instructions and agree on it. The repeated phrase ‘under the hand of Ithamar’ links verse 28 and verse 33.
